evidence.text: Approved role facts, version 2: Northstar Research is a wholly fictional research organisation. Role: Computational Biologist, Atlas team. The team builds reproducible analyses that combine experimental metadata with research datasets. The new colleague will design analysis workflows, investigate inconsistent annotations and collaborate with laboratory scientists and data engineers. Required experience: applied statistical analysis, Python or R, and reproducible research workflows. Location: Bristol; hybrid working with two planned on-site collaboration days per week. No fully remote arrangement or salary range has been approved for this example. Fictional application address: https://careers.northstar.example/atlas-computational-biologist. Team lead interview: Our difficulty is not a lack of data. Different experiments describe samples differently, so apparently comparable analyses can use incompatible groups. We need someone who enjoys tracing those inconsistencies and making the analysis reproducible. The computational biologist will work with the people who generated the data and help agree analysis assumptions. We can describe that collaboration, but we cannot promise a particular publication, promotion timetable or clinical impact.

Help shape the future of research at Northstar Research. We are looking for an experienced Computational Biologist to join Atlas, a collaborative team turning research data into insight. You will build reproducible analyses, work with laboratory scientists and data engineers, and help improve the way experimental information is used. Bring experience in applied statistics, Python or R, and reproducible workflows. The role is based in Bristol, with two planned on-site collaboration days each week. If you want to contribute to meaningful research alongside colleagues with different expertise, read the role description and apply: https://careers.northstar.example/atlas-computational-biologist.

The facts and working arrangement are right. For experienced computational biologists, please lead with the concrete analysis problem and the contribution they would make. Based in Bristol, the role includes two planned on-site collaboration days each week. Explore the work and apply: https://careers.northstar.example/atlas-computational-biologist.

The engineer will build and maintain ingestion pipelines for experimental datasets, implement schema checks and data lineage, and make failed transfers diagnosable. Relevant experience: production Python, SQL, workflow orchestration and maintaining data systems with scientific users. Location: Manchester; three on-site team days per week. Engineering lead note: Small changes to incoming file structures can currently break a research workflow far downstream. The new engineer will add checks where data enters the platform and preserve lineage so colleagues can locate failures. Some days involve pipeline code; others involve agreeing a usable schema with researchers. Please retain the terms schema validation and data lineage because they describe the actual work.

Make a difference through data at Northstar Research. Atlas is looking for an experienced Research Data Engineer to support scientific teams with dependable data systems. You will build ingestion pipelines, add schema validation and data lineage, and work with researchers to diagnose failed transfers. We welcome experience in production Python, SQL and workflow orchestration. The role is based in Manchester, with three on-site team days each week. Help colleagues use experimental datasets with greater confidence. Read the full description and apply: https://careers.northstar.example/atlas-data-engineer.
